humanities_role_explanation: People biographies sampled from Wikidata/Wikipedia supply the generation prompts, but the competence tested is general long-form factual precision of LMs, not disciplinary humanities competence (history, biography as a scholarly genre). The paper itself frames biographies as a convenient objective domain and shows a proof of concept on NLP papers.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text only: prompts ('Tell me a bio of <entity>'), model-generated biographies, atomic facts, and Wikipedia passages.
analytical_tasks_explanation: LMs generate biographies (generation); generations are decomposed into atomic facts (information_extraction in the sense of fact decomposition) and each fact is labelled Supported / Not-supported / Irrelevant against English Wikipedia (fact_verification; paper's 'factual precision' / 'atomic fact precision'). Estimators validate facts via retrieval plus LM. An appendix also explores editing of erroneous sentences.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task: factual precision of long-form biography generation against Wikipedia.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: InstructGPT, ChatGPT, PerplexityAI (human-evaluated); GPT-4, Vicuna, Alpaca, Dolly, Oasst-pythia, StableLM-tuned, MPT Chat (estimated).

quantitative_metrics.note: FActScore (percent of supported atomic facts), error rate, F1 micro, Pearson correlation, inter-annotator agreement.

summary: The paper introduces FActScore, which decomposes LM-generated text into atomic facts and computes the fraction supported by a knowledge source, here Wikipedia for people biographies. It reports human evaluation of InstructGPT, ChatGPT and PerplexityAI, and an automated retrieval+LM estimator with under 2% error used to score 13 further subjects.
key_findings: Human-evaluated FActScores: InstructGPT 42.5, ChatGPT 58.3, PerplexityAI 71.5. Scores drop sharply for rarer entities and for later positions in a generation. The automated estimator has error rate below 2% in the best cases; retrieval helps considerably. GPT-4 and ChatGPT are more factual than public models, and all LMs are less factual than human-written bios.
dataset_size: 183 annotated people entities (human-annotated generations); plus 500 entities x 13 subjects = 6,500 unlabeled generations
evaluation_unit: people entity (biography prompt; one generation per LM per entity, each split into atomic facts)
facets_explanation: Labels were produced by Upwork freelancers recruited as fact-checking experts (qualification test, 2 hours), who validated each atomic fact against English Wikipedia; they are fact-checkers, not humanities scholars, so domain_expert is a loose fit. Facts are judged against Wikipedia, which is not in the stimulus. Disagreement (88-96% agreement on a 10% overlap) is analysed as annotation debatability but treated as a limitation to minimize under the 'undebatable' assumption.
results_explanation: Table 1 reports FActScore of 'InstructGPT 42.5', 'ChatGPT 58.3', 'PerplexityAI 71.5'; the best subject among the originally human-evaluated LMs is PerplexityAI at 71.5 (FActScore, not accuracy, hence metric 'other'). Input-type comparisons exist (no-context vs retrieval estimators, e.g. F1 micro 40.0 vs 87.5 for ChatGPT evaluator on InstructGPT, a gap of 47.5 points), but the main FActScore headline is not a format comparison, so no single gap value is given. Human-written bios are included as a comparison subject in Figure 3 but no numeric score is stated in text, so human_gap_points is null. The 'human baseline' here is a human-bio subject and inter-annotator agreement (96%, 90%, 88%), not a quantified same-metric score.

humanities_role.quote: We evaluate FACTSCORE on the task of generating people biographies because generations consist of verifiable statements rather than debatable or subjective ones

dataset_size.quote: We sample 183 people entities from Wikidata who have corresponding Wikipedia pages.
In total, we evaluate 6,500 generations from 13 subjects

evaluation_set_size.quote: We sample 183 people entities from Wikidata who have corresponding Wikipedia pages.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: The validation is based on zero-shot prompting of an LM referred to as an LMEVAL

gold_source.quote: We recruit fact-checking experts—freelancers who mentioned fact-checking as their expertise—for Step 3.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: they validate the fact based on the English Wikipedia, and label either Supported or Not-supported.

answer_multiplicity.quote: assigning a binary label to each atomic fact

plurality_treatment.quote: Nonetheless, since our agreement rate is fairly high (91%), we think such cases are rare in our particular domain of people biographies.

human_baseline_reported.quote: The agreement rates are 96%, 90% and 88% for InstructGPT, ChatGPT and PerplexityAI, respectively.
